SPN manages and operates 26 television channels, the streaming media platform [[SonyLIV]], as well as the television studio Studio NEXT and film studio Sony Pictures Networks Productions.{{Cite web|url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/enterprise/sony-pictures-new-revenue-avenues-after-ipl/103691|title=Sony Pictures Networks: Life after IPL|website=Fortune India|date=4 November 2019 |language=en|access-date=2020-02-25|archive-date=18 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218003135/https://www.fortuneindia.com/enterprise/sony-pictures-new-revenue-avenues-after-ipl/103691|url-status=live}} ==History== It was founded on 30 September 1995{{Cite web|title=SET India Private Limited Information - SET India Private Limited Company Profile, SET India Private Limited News on The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/company/set-india-private-limited/U99999DL1995PTC072517|access-date=2021-10-15|website=The Economic Times|archive-date=24 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211024173608/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/company/set-india-private-limited/U99999DL1995PTC072517|url-status=live}} as Sony Entertainment Television India Private Limited (SET India Pvt Ltd.).{{Cite web|title=NP Singh is Multi Screen Media CEO|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/np-singh-is-multi-screen-media-ceo/article23172198.ece|access-date=2021-10-14|website=@businessline|date=3 January 2014|language=en|archive-date=29 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029174849/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/np-singh-is-multi-screen-media-ceo/article23172198.ece|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|title=SET INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED - Company, directors and contact details|website=Zauba Corp|url=https://www.zaubacorp.com/company/SET-INDIA-PRIVATE-LIMITED/U99999DL1995PTC072517|access-date=2021-10-15|archive-date=29 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029180121/https://www.zaubacorp.com/company/SET-INDIA-PRIVATE-LIMITED/U99999DL1995PTC072517|url-status=live}} The first channel from the company was [[Sony Entertainment Television]]. In 1999, SET India Pvt Ltd., launched its second channel [[Sony Max]]{{Cite web|title="We are getting into an aggressive growth mode now"- N.P. Singh|url=https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/45930_we-are-getting-into-an-aggressive-growth-mode-now--np-singh|access-date=2021-10-14|website=afaqs!|archive-date=28 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028165311/https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/45930_we-are-getting-into-an-aggressive-growth-mode-now--np-singh|url-status=live}} which broadcast Hindi movies and sports events along with Sony Entertainment Television. In 2005, SET India Network bought SAB TV from Sri Adhikari Brothers and rebranded as [[Sony SAB]].{{Cite web|date=2005-03-15|title=Adhikaris sell SAB TV brand to Sony for $13 m|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/archive/adhikaris-sell-sab-tv-brand-to-sony-for-13-m/128751/|access-date=2021-10-14|website=The Financial Express|language=en-US|archive-date=20 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020100520/https://www.financialexpress.com/archive/adhikaris-sell-sab-tv-brand-to-sony-for-13-m/128751/|url-status=live}} In 2006 SET India launched the English movie channel [[Sony Pix]]. In December 2007, SET India Private Limited was renamed as Multi Screen Media Private Limited.{{Cite web|title=SET India renamed Multi Screen Media Pvt. Ltd|url=https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/20025_set-india-renamed-multi-screen-media-pvt-ltd|access-date=2021-10-14|website=afaqs!|archive-date=28 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028165313/https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/20025_set-india-renamed-multi-screen-media-pvt-ltd|url-status=live}} In December 2015, the company was renamed as Sony Pictures Networks India (SPN).{{Cite news|url=https://www.exchange4media.com/media-tv-news/multi-screen-mediamsm-is-now-sony-pictures-networks-indiaspn-62676.html|title=Multi Screen Media (MSM) is now Sony Pictures Networks India (SPN)|newspaper=Indian Advertising Media & Marketing News – Exchange4Media|language=en|date=14 December 2015|access-date=2020-02-25|archive-date=25 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225184228/https://www.exchange4media.com/media-tv-news/multi-screen-mediamsm-is-now-sony-pictures-networks-indiaspn-62676.html|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|last=Shah|first=Gouri|date=2014-01-03|title=N.P. Singh takes over as CEO at Multi-Screen Media|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/DwGXjREmMR6WkyS3fvYQcO/NP-Singh-takes-over-as-CEO-at-MSML.html|access-date=2021-10-14|website=mint|language=en|archive-date=29 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029171537/https://www.livemint.com/Companies/DwGXjREmMR6WkyS3fvYQcO/NP-Singh-takes-over-as-CEO-at-MSML.html|url-status=live}} On 24 October 2022, nearly all of Sony's networks underwent a rebranding coinciding with [[Diwali]], replacing the cropped "S" logo used by SET since its launch with the S-curve logo template used by Sony's television networks worldwide since 2019, and first used locally by SonyLIV.{{Cite web |title=Sony Pictures Networks India Rebrands Channel Portfolio |url=https://www.businessworld.in/article/Sony-Pictures-Networks-India-Rebrands-Channel-Portfolio/25-10-2022-451574 |access-date=2022-10-25 |website=BW Businessworld |language=en }}{{Dead link|date=July 2023}} === Attempted merger with Zee === On 22 September 2021, [[Zee Entertainment Enterprises]] announced that it had reached an agreement in principle to merge its television networks, production operations, digital assets, and program libraries with SPN; the combined company would be majority-owned by Sony, and led by Zee CEO [[Punit Goenka]].{{Cite web |title=Zee Entertainment Approves In-principle Merger With Sony Pictures India |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/zee-entertainment-signs-merger-deal-with-sony-pictures-india-7492871.html |access-date=2021-10-21 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en |archive-date=21 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021143533/https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/zee-entertainment-signs-merger-deal-with-sony-pictures-india-7492871.html |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |title=Sony Pictures India to Merge With Zee Entertainment |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/zee-to-merge-with-sony-pictures-india-1235018372 |access-date=2021-09-21 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en |archive-date=22 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210922151655/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/zee-to-merge-with-sony-pictures-india-1235018372/ |url-status=live }} On 21 December 2021, the two companies reached a definitive agreement to merge; it was stated that the combined company "should be well-positioned to meet the growing consumer demand for premium content across entertainment touchpoints and platform[s]."{{cite web |date=22 December 2021 |title=Sony Pictures Networks, Zee Complete Merger to Create Indian TV Giant |url=https://variety.com/2021/global/news/sony-pictures-networks-zee-merger-complete-1235140626/ |access-date=22 December 2021 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |archive-date=22 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222033806/https://variety.com/2021/global/news/sony-pictures-networks-zee-merger-complete-1235140626/ |url-status=live }} Under the agreement, Sony will hold a 51% stake in the combined company, and inherit Zee's public listing on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]].{{Cite web |last1=Ramachandran |first1=Naman |last2=Frater |first2=Patrick |date=2023-08-10 |title=Sony-Zee TV Mega Merger in India Is Given Green Light |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/asia/sony-zee-tv-merger-in-india-1235692955/ |access-date=2023-08-20 |website=Variety |language=en-US}} The companies set a two-year deadline of 21 December 2023 to complete the merger, with a one-month grace period ending 20 January 2024.{{Cite web |last=Ksheerasagar |first=A. |date=2024-01-10 |title=Zee Entertainment stock rebounds, gains over 4%; here's why |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/zee-entertainment-stock-rebounds-gains-over-4-as-company-says-sony-merger-cancellation-report-baseless-11704865683747.html |access-date=2024-01-11 |website=mint |language=en}} In 2022, SPN changed its corporate name to Culver Max Entertainment Pvt. Ltd.; the name is used exclusively by the holding company, which continues to otherwise do business as Sony Pictures Networks.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-04 |title=Zee-Sony merger wins CCI approval with modifications |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/zeesony-merger-wins-cci-approval-with-modifications-11664906869572.html |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=mint |language=en}} In October 2022, the merger was approved by the [[Competition Commission of India]] (CCI); it was reported that Zee had voluntarily agreed to divest or shut down one general entertainment channel as a condition of the approval. In June 2023, the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] (SEBI) prohibited Goenka from holding directorial positions in any listed company for one year, amid an investigation into allegations of [[insider trading]]; the action was considered to be a potential impediment to the closure of the merger, as he was expected to lead the combined company {{Cite web |last=Ramachandran |first=Naman |date=2023-10-31 |title=Sony-Zee $10 Billion Merger Back on Track After Regulator Ban on MD Punit Goenka Lifted |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/asia/punit-goenka-ban-sony-zee-merger-1235773910/ |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-06-13 |title=Zee shares fall 6% after Sebi order on Subhash Chandra, Punit Goenka |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/after-sebi-order-on-subhash-chandra-punit-goenka-zee-share-price-to-be-in-focus-11686624851405.html |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=Livemint |language=en}}{{Cite web |last1=Frater |first1=Naman Ramachandran, Patrick |last2=Ramachandran |first2=Naman |last3=Frater |first3=Patrick |date=2023-06-13 |title=Punit Goenka, Subhash Chandra Barred by Regulators From Holding Management Positions at Zee, as Sony Merger Looms |url=https://variety.com/2023/global/global/zee-punit-goenka-subhash-chandra-sebi-ban-sony-1235641034/ |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=Variety |language=en-US}} On 10 August 2023, the merger was approved by the [[National Company Law Tribunal]] (NCLT). In September 2023, Sony stated that the merger would be delayed for unspecified reasons.{{Cite web |last=Ramachandran |first=Naman |date=2023-09-29 |title=Sony-Zee Merger Delayed – Global Bulletin |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/asia/sony-zee-merger-delay-1235739854/ |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=Variety |language=en-US}} In November 2023, the SEBI lifted its ban on Goenka after an appeal. On 9 January 2024, amid rumors that Sony was seeking to call off the merger, Zee issued a statement that it was still committed to completing the agreement, and called the reports "baseless". However, on 22 January 2024, Sony issued a notice to Zee effectively terminating the merger proceedings due to, among other reasons, the closing conditions to the merger not being satisfied by the given deadline of 21 January.{{cite web|title=Sony Calls Off $10 Billion Merger With Indian TV Giant Zee Entertainment Enterprises|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|first1=Patrick|last1=Frater|first2=Naman|last2=Ramachandran|date=22 January 2024|access-date=22 January 2024|url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/sony-zee-india-deal-halted-1235865873/}} ==Sports== {{Main|Sony Sports Network}} The network forayed into the Indian sports TV market in 2002 after acquiring the media rights for [[International Cricket Council|International Cricket Council (ICC)]] matches from 2002 to 2007,{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Sony-bags-World-Cup-TV-rights/articleshow/1093996.cms|title=Sony bags World Cup TV rights|website=The Times of India|date=15 February 2002|access-date=16 April 2018|archive-date=16 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180416013044/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Sony-bags-World-Cup-TV-rights/articleshow/1093996.cms|url-status=live}} which were broadcast on SET and Sony MAX.{{Cite web|url=https://www.exchange4media.com/TV/Sony-to-air-ICC-Champion%e2%80%99s-Trophy-on-MAX-and-SET-no-plans-for-sports-channel._5159.html|title=Sony to air ICC Champion's Trophy on MAX and SET, no plans for sports channel|website=exchange4media|date=4 April 2002|access-date=16 April 2018|archive-date=16 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180416073554/https://www.exchange4media.com/TV/Sony-to-air-ICC-Champion%e2%80%99s-Trophy-on-MAX-and-SET-no-plans-for-sports-channel._5159.html|url-status=live}} SET / Sony MAX were known for animated Tiger sequences during the live TV match events of ICC Cricket World Cup 2003 - 2007 & ICC Champions Trophy 2006, for example Tiger do Bangra dance when batter hits a six. Sony Max referred the animation as the Deewana Tiger (Mascot) for the channel. {{Cite news |date=2003-02-26 |title=For Vivekananda, it's a tiger's tale for the World Cup |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/calcutta-times/for-vivekananda-its-a-tigers-tale-for-the-world-cup/articleshow/38604895.cms |access-date=2024-08-03 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}} The animation was the brainchild of Vivekananda Roy Ghatak & it was created by 2NZAnimation for the Sony Max. {{Cite web |title=Up close with 2nz CEO & Climb Media Creative Director Kireet Khurana - |url=https://www.animationxpress.com/interviews/up-close-with-2nz-ceo-climb-media-creative-director-kireet-khurana/ |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=www.animationxpress.com|date=21 June 2004 }} In Sony Pictures Networks India Private Limited (SPN or SPNI) is an Indian media conglomerate owned by Sony Pictures Entertainment.
SPN manages and operates 26 television channels, the streaming media platform SonyLIV, as well as the television studio Studio NEXT and film studio Sony Pictures Networks Productions.
